To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the repeated retrieval of means to goals leads to inhibition of competing means.
repeated retrieval of a target means causes inhibited access to competing means.
repeated retrieval of a goal—means combination leads to inhibition of competing means to the same goal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and how the repeated retrieval of target means causes inhibition of competitors in a multiple means situation.
the cognitive processes underlying goal-directed habits in the context of multiple means and demonstrates that repeated retrieval of target means causes inhibition of competing means.
the question of how habits are formed and maintained and the conditions under which they can be changed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of habits in a multiple goal—means context is a complex process that is not fully captured by a single process model.
the formation of habits is a complex process that is dependent upon the number of times the goal—means combination is retrieved.
habits are goal-directed and that they involve the inhibition of competing means.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
repeated retrieval of a target means upon goal—means combination leads to the formation of a habit, which is characterized by inhibited accessibility to competing means for the goal.
repeated retrieval of target means causes inhibition of competing means and that this process is not dependent on the explicit intent to inhibit.
repeated retrieval of a target means to a goal results in the inhibition of competing means.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of habits in a multiple-means context is not a simple process of strengthening the target means and weakening competing means.
the formation of goal—means associations is not necessarily the formation of an exclusive goal—means network but can also be a process that involves the inhibition of competing means.
the repeated retrieval of a means to a goal can lead to inhibition of the retrieval of competing means.
